"You are what you do, not the lies you tell yourself."

He reaches for an interface, pauses, then speaks.

"Now go away."

"Hah," Orcus Rao says, rolling his eyes. "We got another one."

He makes a shoo motion. "Off with you."

The comms cut.
"You're already signed up with the Hegemony. Good. That saves me a lot of bureaucratic nonsense."

"As you bear the commission of the Persean League..." He makes a half-shrug. "I can't have you in a position of divided loyalty."

"Let us speak again on the matter if your situation changes."

His tone makes it clear that the issue is settled. For now.

"Seeing as you're a full, albeit junior, member of the Persean League we can't have you in a position of divided loyalty, can we."

He produces a little shrug. "Let us speak again on the matter if your situation changes."

His tone makes it clear that the issue is settled. For now.

"Seeing as you're a full, albeit junior, member of the Persean League... well, we can't very well divide your loyalties."

"Besides," a fleeting smile appears. "I see you've fallen into Reynard Hannan's orbit. An ego of that size produces a gravity well which is very difficult to escape."

"Of course."

He sits back, face falling into shadow.
"But you made the deal," Rao says impishly. "You didn't have to."

"Then nothing more need be said."

His tone makes it clear that the conversation is over.

Rao holds a finger to his cheek for a moment, thinking.

"It could be earned," he says. "But that's up to you."

"What admirable loyalty! How Reynard earns it, I've never understood. I must study his leadership closely, for I obviously have much to learn." The sarcasm runs thick.

Rao sits back, face falling into shadow.

"Seeing as you're a full, albeit junior, member of the Persean League... we can't have you in a position of divided loyalty, can we."

He produces a little shrug.

"But perhaps," he looks aside. "We might have a mutual friend on Kazeron?"
"I understand. Keeping with his trust is more important than serving that goal." He leans back, "It's interesting."
Rao raises an eyebrow, his expression amused.

He smiles coyly, leaving your statement deliberately unanswered.

"It is possible our work together would serve certain common goals."

"Although the Hegemony is no stranger to making common cause with the Church of Galactic Redemption..."

He makes a half-shrug.

"You've chosen your path. I couldn't possibly distract you from your god-bothering."

"The Hegemony is no stranger to making common cause with the Church of Galactic Redemption..." He makes a half-shrug.

"I suppose," he says slowly, "If you can put up with me, I can deal with your god-bothering."

"The Hegemony is no stranger to making common cause with the Church of Galactic Redemption..." He makes a half-shrug, then pauses to look right at you.

"It's the guns you've given Standfast," his words are precise, "that convince me of your dedication."

He looks away, casual again. "If you can put up with me, I can deal with your god-bothering."

"Ludd, I think, doesn't need self-appointed curates to shield the Faith from my little comments," he says, his eyes suddenly sharp. "Pray on the matter. I insist."

He leans back, and his face falls into shadow.

"I'd like to offer you work. You don't have to salute me, and I'll make sure you're paid promptly."

He leans forward, his hands together. "What do you think? Could be fun. Play your cards right, and you'll be a legend."

"The truth makes few friends." Rao produces a wry smile.

"I never could stand a fool, especially when they're members of the Strategic Assembly. So," he holds his hand out to indicate his surroundings, Ragnar Complex.

"It's not so bad."

"A proper officer of the Hegemony is taught to leap toward the enemy, blazing guns. Once the noise quiets down, they'll wait, slack-jawed, for the medals to get pinned to their uniforms." 

"Such is the way of the Domain, which we must uphold."

He half-raises a finger, a quirk on his lips. "Officially," he concludes.

"Baikal was kind enough to find me a place where I could get important work done. I deal with... let us call them 'unique circumstances'. And for this I find it necessary to have energetic freelancers available."

"I'll ensure you're paid promptly for a roster of small merc jobs."

"Then, perhaps something big will come up. When it does, I want to know I can count on you."

"I'm offering you the chance to be the grit that throws history off its axis."

He lets a sly smile fade. "There are many bodies of power turning just now. Slowly grinding away, warships and bombings and riots and resources."

"The Persean Sector needs change, or it will grind what's left of us to dust."

A cold, quick expression passes over his face.

"Let us say that I'd be as satisfied as any Hegemony officer to cut down that pompous traitor. Setting aside even the matter of honor, I have a personal dislike of the man."

Rao lets out a slow breath. "That's talk for old comrades, over drink."

He leans back, not quite committing to a frown.

"Patience, captain."

"There's rules to break when you need to win, and there's betrayal. These are very different things, fundamentally so, captain. He and I have done the former, but he threw away his honor with the latter."

"We are not. the. same." Rao's words come out slow, and cold.
"Good," his approval comes with a sly smile. "Have your people set up secure comms. We'll show the Strategic Assembly how it's done."

"Let us speak again on the matter if your situation changes."

His tone makes it clear that the issue is settled. For now.

"Nothing more need be said."

His tone makes it clear that the conversation is over.

The comms-link takes a moment to establish. Skiron adjusts the feed parameters as she greets you, clearly unused to holo-comms.

"Captain. Your crew have been most helpful in establishing a colonial comms network. Have you been able to reach Command? We are most anxious to receive new orders, especially given our upgraded capacities."

The comms-link takes a moment to establish. Skiron adjusts the feed parameters as she greets you.

"Greetings captain. All proceeds in accordance with protocol."

"Of course; the Protocols are-" She catches herself and looks just a little embarrassed. "I mean to say, we continue to follow the principles, yes. We are receiving updated training to bring the settlement in line with current doctrine, as per the personal request of the High Hegemon."

She sits up just a little straighter, as if Baikal Daud is, perhaps, keeping an eye on her.

"I would like to extend the thanks of myself and our colony for your technical assistance," Commander Skiron beams as she speaks.

"The crew you left with us are ready to return to your $shipOrFleet; my quartermaster shall coordinate transport with your subordinates," she says.

"Well, ah. Most of them will be returning. A few have come to... other accommodations in their time among us, and we honor their contribution to our world."

$HeOrShe blinks at you.

"Why're you talking to me, then? Call her yourself," $heOrShe says with a snort.
OR
"Kanta? Ha-ha, I'll just ask if she's free."

$HeOrShe lets that hang for a moment.

"You get hit on the head? You don't just - talk - to the Warlord. Need's you a real good reason. Anyway, not up to me," $heOrShe crosses $hisOrHer arms. "Ask the station king."
OR
"Yeah? That'll have to be too bad 'cause I just do my bit, and if she wants something, someone tells me. Only goes one way."

$HeOrShe leans back, satisfied with that explanation.
OR
"Talk to the station king," $heOrShe says brusquely. "Not for me to say who gets to see the pirate queen."

The vid feed flickers to life, a wash of static and audio distortion receding as your datapad adjusts for outdated comm protocols.

"Yeah, who're you?" $personName snarls before bothering to glance at a grimy datapad. "Ah," $hisOrHer demeanor shifts hostility down several levels. "You again. Right, right."

The portking of Kanta's Den appears before you with all of $hisOrHer singular charm. "You blasted, bloody rad-addled fool! You think you can vac-drop the Warlord's pet then just dance yourself back into her home? Them is some brassies you've got $playerName, but you got 'em instead of brains. I almost respect it."

$HeOrShe spits, the projectile presumably landing on $hisOrHer own control interface, "But only almost. Meantime, I'll be sittin' and smilin' watching all Kanta's underbosses fight for the chance to slag your flagship."
After an exceptionally rude gesture, the comms cut out.

The pilot goes through routine chatter with what passes for traffic control. At the point that control asks for the standard bribe for a good landing slot, you have comms control forwarded to your datapad.

"Yeh, who's this then, shuttle?" control crackles, "Gonna buy me lunch, or do you like waiting?"
The pilot goes through routine chatter with what passes for traffic control. A previous bribe means you're recognized and get you a direct comms request to the station king, no waiting.
